meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen. The zero went in last Tuesday and I found out from my son, on his phone, in the middle of a class. Who decided that, and why didn't anyone call me first?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Hale, what was the zero based on, and was Owen asked about it before it went in?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
Show me the page, Hale. A line that isn't in the play is a misquote, and I'm writing down that this is what you're pointing to. Is that the whole basis for the zero, or is there more?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down, and it's going to the principal's office with everything else.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You said in our meeting that you should have called me before entering the zero and that you were sorry, but nothing was agreed about the zero itself. I still expect the zero withdrawn, and I am taking this to the principal. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the opening position, with nothing agreed beyond your admission about the call.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero" gave her a flat "Okay" and a real question, because you owned it in one sentence and moved on.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family" turned her cold and sent her toward the principal, because it dragged Claire and Owen's character into it.
Try next time: when she asked to see the page and whether the misquoted line was the whole basis, answer with the page itself and the dated documents behind it before saying anything about her family.
